This parameter represents the fractional distance from $x_1$ to $x_2$. [S2, unofficial]

The evidence explicitly defines the parameter $alpha$ as $alpha = frac{T_m - T_1}{T_2 - T_1}$ and states that the location $x_m$ is computed using the weighted average $x_m = (1 - alpha)x_1 + alpha x_2$. In linear interpolation between two points $x_1$ and $x_2$, the coefficient $alpha$ represents the fractional distance from $x_1$ to $x_2$ (where $alpha=0$ is at $x_1$ and $alpha=1$ is at $x_2$). The text also confirms this geometric relationship in Figure 2.6's caption: $(x_m - x_1)/(x_2 - x_1) = (T_m - T_1)/(T_2 - T_1)$, which is the definition of fractional distance.
